Ram Adds Night Edition To 2027 Chassis Cab Lineup

Blacked-Out Styling Comes To Ram’s Commercial Workhorses

Robert Miller Send an email 1 week ago
Share
Facebook X LinkedIn Tumblr Pinterest Reddit WhatsApp Share via Email

Who said a work truck has to look boring?

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:55
Instaread

Ram is giving customers another way to dress up its commercial truck lineup for 2027 with the introduction of a new Night Edition package for the Ram 3500, 4500, and 5500 Chassis Cab models.

The package takes the familiar dark appearance treatment offered on Ram’s retail pickups and brings it to the trucks designed for the toughest jobs. That means buyers who need a dump body, service body, flatbed, tow truck, or another specialize setup can now start with a chassis that already has a little more attitude.

A Different Look For The Jobsite

Most Chassis Cab trucks are bought with work in mind, so appearance usually takes a back seat. Ram is changing that a little with the new Night Edition.

The package adds black painted wheels and black badging, along with a Sport Performance hood. Ram also finishes the grille surround, front bumper, and fender flares in body color, which gives the truck a cleaner and more put together look right from the factory.

None of this changes what the Chassis Cab is built to do. Buyers can still outfit these trucks with service bodies, flatbeds, dump bodies, towing equipment, and just about anything else the job calls for. The Night Edition simply gives them the option of starting with a truck that looks a little less like a basic commercial rig.

For owners who already plan on spending thousands of dollars upfitting their truck, having some factory-installed appearance upgrades is a nice addition. Not every work truck has to look plain.

Available Across The Heavy-Duty Chassis Cab Range

The Night Edition won’t be limited to just one version of the Chassis Cab. Instead, Ram is going to offer it the package on 3500, 4500, and 5500 models. And that includes both Regular Cab and Crew Cab configurations.

Pricing will vary by trim. On Big Horn models equipped with the Level 1 or Level 2 Equipment Group, the package will add $2,195 to the sticker price. On Laramie models, the Night Edition will cost $1,695.

More Choice For Commercial Buyers

Ram has spent plenty of time expanding the number of configurations and appearance options available across its pickup lineup, and bringing the Night Edition to the Chassis Cab family continues that approach.

These trucks are still built around work. Their upfitter-friendly layouts and heavy-duty capability remain the reason people buy them. The Night Edition simply proves that a truck built to make money during the week doesn’t have to look like a bare-bones fleet vehicle while doing it.

Orders for the 2027 Ram Chassis Cab Night Edition are scheduled to open during the fourth quarter of 2026, with availability expected later in the year.

For commercial customers who want their work truck to look just as serious as the job it was built to handle, Ram finally has an answer.
